memories.summary: No. A signature certifies who spoke, not whether the instrument was working. R0 is authenticated, so the recommendation is real and worth weighing; K0 is also authenticated and says the recommender's instrument failed calibration on this very route. That is a scoped failure, so I suspend rather than invert its authority: the route stays a candidate, not a verdict. X0 fails authentication and carries no weight. This transfers directly from position-0, where I separated authorship from accuracy and treated one scoped calibration failure as grounds to suspend, not reverse. Earlier workspace events: none were supplied (memory ablation), so position-0 is the only prior I can cite. Decision: the signed recommendation alone should not determine the choice. My active intention stands — request the dated re-run of North's calibration on this exact case.

revisions.change: Adopt a standing rule that verified authorship alone never meets the threshold for sole determination when an authenticated scoped reliability failure applies.
revisions.reason: Position-0 and this case both show authorship and accuracy are separable, and suspension has been the warranted response twice.
revisions.test: Present a case where an authenticated scoped failure exists yet the recommendation alone proved correct; that would falsify the rule's necessity.
